title: Roast celeriac and chickpeas with tahini

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or a simple single-ingredient staple such as tinned chickpeas and tahini, with no jars, stock pots or packet mixes.

supermarket.reason: Celeriac, kale, chickpeas, tahini and pumpkin seeds are all everyday items at Tesco and similar shops.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a roasting tray, a bowl and a whisk, and the roasting technique is beginner-friendly.

works.reason: A whole celeriac, two tins of chickpeas and the kale make a generous traybake for four, roasted for 36 minutes at 220°C with a properly seasoned dressing.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes is fair for peeling and cubing a celeriac, cutting onion wedges, tearing kale and slicing an apple, and the 36 cook minutes match the 20+10+6 in the steps.

honest_ingredients.reason: The seasoning list gives smoked paprika but step 1 says '1 tsp paprika', which is a separate cupboard item, so a reader with both may reach for the wrong one.

seasonal_feel.reason: A hot roast celeriac traybake suits mid-November, and the celeriac is the bulk and point of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are plain, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Roast vegetables, chickpeas, kale and a tahini dressing make a filling, balanced lunch that a family would happily eat again.
